data.title: Moodboard
data.tagline: A moodboard collects reference images, colors, and keywords on one board—align on "what feeling" before building the page.
data.learningOutcome: You can replace adjectives with a reference collage, and include dislikes to draw the boundary.
data.description: "Make it premium" or "give it breathing room" rarely means the same thing to you and the AI. Collect five or six screenshots you like, one or two you dislike, and the main color, then send the collage—working from pictures lands far closer than adjectives. Fixing a wrong direction at the collage stage means swapping a reference; after the page is built, it means redoing the work.

learning.assumes: You have saved screenshots of websites you like, or sent a "make it feel like this" image to a designer.
learning.outcome: You can replace adjectives with a reference collage, and include dislikes to draw the boundary.

distinctions.label: Wireframe
distinctions.explanation: Wireframe settles structure—what sits where; Moodboard settles feeling—what it should look like before that.

distinctions.label: Minimalism
distinctions.explanation: Minimalism is one concrete style; Moodboard is the tool for choosing whichever style fits, references included.

explanation.title: Liked references
explanation.text: Three to five screenshots of pages or posters you like. Any source works—competitors or other industries—so long as the "feeling" is right.

explanation.title: Disliked counter-examples
explanation.text: Include one clearly wrong direction and mark it. AIs are great imitators; exclusions help more than adjectives.

explanation.title: Main color and keywords
explanation.text: Circle the color to use and write two or three mood words ("quiet," "paper-like"). Images set the direction; words refine it.

data.boundary: A moodboard is not a wireframe—it fixes "what feeling," not "what goes where"; use them in sequence: board for direction, wireframe for structure. References are not templates to copy: tell the AI "capture the mood, don't copy the layout." AI-generated images can serve as references too, though real site screenshots often land closer to buildable results.

lessonPractice.title: The AI's site style keeps missing what you want after four rounds. Which move most likely aligns it in one shot?

options.label: Paste three screenshots you like plus one you dislike, and send them together
options.feedback: Correct. Likes set the direction, the crossed-out one draws the boundary. Solving direction at the collage stage avoids redoing finished work.

options.label: Keep describing in words: "more premium, more minimal"
options.feedback: "Premium" and "minimal" have no shared definition; round five will drift the same way.

options.label: Have the AI generate five random palettes and pick a good one
options.feedback: All five build on an unstated direction; picking a hit would be luck, not alignment.

data.agentPrompt: Follow the references I sent: the three liked ones set the feel, avoid the crossed-out one, and use the main color I circled. Show me a hero screenshot before continuing.
